request: Why does recursive feature elimination refit after each drop?

composition.story: Recursive feature elimination removes the weakest feature iteratively. Refitting after each drop ensures the remaining feature coefficients update correctly for the next ranking step.

aha.observation: Coefficient weights shift dramatically when a correlated feature is removed, proving that refitting is essential for accurate ranking.

states.label: Full Model
states.sentence: Fit estimator on all available features.
states.why: Establishes baseline coefficients for all variables.

states.label: Drop Weakest
states.sentence: Identify and remove Feature B with the lowest coefficient.
states.why: Removes noise from the feature space.

states.label: Refit Weights
states.sentence: Refit the model on remaining features A and C.
states.why: Uncovers updated coefficients affected by multicollinearity.
